sources.citation: 刀洁 scholar profile, 中国民族语言学网 cneling.com/scholardetail-64.htm (publication list: 金平傣语概况, 金平傣语语音的演变, 守望国境线上的家园——金平傣族的社会文化 2007, etc.).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; confirms further Jinping Dai phonology papers by Dao Jie (e.g. 金平傣语语音的演变) exist in Chinese journals, none open.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A.; Gregerson, Kenneth J.; Nguyen Van Loi. n.d. [c. 2000]. Borderlands: Lesser Known Indigenous Languages of Northern Vietnam -- Map & Language Descriptions (University of Texas at Arlington project web page; Wayback Machine 2015 capture).
sources.note: Nothing. Section 'P. Padi [pa31 zi31]' says Padi is a SW Tai language of Muong Khuong (Lao Cai), ~300 speakers, 'in terms of tone splits, tone values, phonology, and lexicon coincidentally very similar to Central Thai of Bangkok'; cites Abadie 1924 and L-Thongkum (1998) for varieties in China. No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2007. The power of language over the past: Tai settlement and Tai linguistics in southern China and northern Vietnam. 25 pp. (author's PDF, Wayback capture of uta.edu/faculty/jerry/).
sources.note: Nothing; full text layer searched, no mention of Padi/Pa Di.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 1998. The language corridor: New evidence from Vietnam. In Somsonge Burusphat (ed.), Proceedings of the International Conference on Tai Studies, 129-150. Bangkok: ILCRD, Mahidol University. (SEAlang SALA scan, image-only; scanned at 300 dpi.)
sources.note: Nothing on Pa Di: the paper treats Kadai, Kam, Sui and Giay (Bouyei) of the borderlands; Padi is not discussed.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Pa Di language' and Wikipedia (vi) 'Tiếng Pa Dí' / 'Người Pa Dí' (read for bibliography and identity only).
sources.note: Nothing; only 'Pa Di tonal splits are similar to those of Standard Thai' (from Edmondson). References are ethnographic (Bùi Quốc Khánh 2013; Ngô Đức Thịnh 1975; Yunnan minzu shibie report 1960/1979) plus Edmondson's web page.
